title: The Signs a Team Is Waiting for a Decision or Strategy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article diagnoses a common but often misread symptom: a team that seems sluggish, over-meets, and lacks urgency may simply be waiting on a decision or strategic direction that hasn't yet materialized. Because leaders themselves aren't waiting — they already understand the pending ambiguity — they can misread the team's hesitancy as burnout, overwhelm, or disengagement rather than a rational response to uncertainty. The piece uses leadership transitions as a clear example of this dynamic and argues that simply asking the team what they need to move faster will often surface the real cause. It closes by reminding leaders that teams usually just need repetition and clarity, not a wholesale re-motivation effort.
points: Sluggish, low-urgency teams may be waiting on a pending decision or strategy rather than lacking motivation.
Leaders can misread this waiting as burnout, distraction, or disengagement because they themselves aren't waiting.
Leadership transitions are a clear example of teams deliberately slowing down amid uncertainty.
Simply asking team members what they need often reveals they are waiting for clarity from above.
Most of the time, teams just need repetition of an existing strategy, not a brand-new motivational push.
quotes: Leaders sometimes wonder why their team isn’t acting aggressively, working with urgency, or executing with vigor.
Teams and team members waiting for a decision or strategy often appear as if they are in suspended animation for a reason—they are!
Teams are the least productive during leadership transitions for a good reason. They don’t want to waste their time pursuing outcomes a new leader may not find critical or important.
Compounding matters, a team waiting for clarity or a path forward is often misread by leaders.
As a rule, teams are always wanting and waiting for more clarity from those above.
